title: Cross-language SDK resilience: granular retries, resumable streams, and pagination composition
creator: Ayesha Patel
description: Deliver a cross-language requirements set and acceptance criteria for SDK behaviors around retries, pagination, and streaming so Python/TypeScript/Go clients behave consistently and safely in production. This ticket covers API-level contracts (idempotency, cursor tokens, stream checkpoints), client ergonomics (iterators, backpressure hooks), and compatibility constraints for server-side versioning.
background: Multiple customer incidents and internal experiments show a gap between SDKs when handling partial failures during long-running streaming responses and when combining paginated endpoints with transforms (e.g., map+filter across pages). Existing PRDs address streaming and pagination separately; we need a consolidated compatibility contract so app developers can migrate SDK versions without surprising behavior.
goals: 1) Define deterministic retry semantics (idempotency keys, retry windows) for unary and streaming endpoints across Python/TS/Go. 2) Define a resumable streaming protocol for partial-response checkpointing and client resume semantics. 3) Specify pagination composition semantics (cursor token stability, backfill safety) and client iterators/APIs for sync/async usage. 4) Provide concrete acceptance tests and test vectors that each SDK implementation must pass.
non_goals: 1) Implementation work in each SDK (this ticket is requirements + acceptance criteria only). 2) Changes to server-side token formats (we will specify compatibility constraints but server change requests are separate).
requirements:
- Retry semantics: define at-least-once vs at-most-once guarantees, idempotency token formats, exponential backoff defaults, and absolute retry windows.
- Streaming resume: server must return opaque resume tokens at safe checkpoints; clients must expose resume() API that accepts the token plus an optional requested-range parameter; client libraries must surface partial-result callbacks.
- Pagination: standardize an opaque 'page_token' cursor with stability guarantees (token valid for N hours; server must allow deterministic forward-only reads; token revocation semantics documented).
- Client iterators: Python/Go synchronous iterators and async/Promise-based iterators in TS that hide cursor handling but allow access to raw tokens for manual resume.
- Composition semantics: When a user composes pagination with client-side transforms (map, filter), document whether transforms are applied per-page or as a streaming pipeline; default should be pipeline semantics with memory-bound safeguards.
- Compatibility: New SDK minor versions must be backward compatible with previous token formats for at least 6 months or provide a migration helper. Breaking changes require documented migration steps and feature flags.
- Observability hooks: each SDK should expose hooks for token-level latency, retry counters, and resume attempts to integrate with Console tracing.
scope_changes:
- 2026-03-12: Narrowed scope to requirements + acceptance criteria; moved implementation tasks to separate ENG tickets.
- 2026-03-13: Added requirement for explicit observability hooks after PM/Eng sync.
- 2026-03-14: Reduced initial compatibility guarantee from 12 months to 6 months after legal/ops feedback.
acceptance_criteria:
1) A language-agnostic spec document exists (Confluence) describing retry timelines, idempotency tokens, and resume-token format constraints.
2) A test harness with at least eight test vectors (interleaved failure, truncated streams, token expiry, multi-page transforms) is defined and automated.
3) Example pseudocode for Python/TS/Go showing iterator/resume/retry usage is included.
4) Compatibility policy documented with migration guidance and a 'compatibility-check' checklist.
5) PM, Eng, and DX review approvals recorded in PRD comments.
test_plan:
- Author canonical test scenarios and expected semantics as plain JSON fixtures.
- Run fixtures against a mock server that can inject failures (partial-response cut, token rotation, delayed ack).
- Each SDK implementation must run fixture suite and submit results as a CI artifact.
- Include manual exploratory tests for composition (map+filter across pages) and long-running streams (>10 minutes) to validate resume semantics.
rollout_plan: 1) Publish spec and test fixtures to internal Confluence + shared test repo. 2) Create per-language ENG tickets to implement client behavior and CI gate. 3) Ship acceptance-tests-only in sdk-2026.04 and require passing CI before promoting to public releases. 4) Communicate compatibility window to customers via changelog and migration guide.
open_questions: Should resume tokens be opaque or include a signed epoch for server-side validation?
What is the maximum retention window for page tokens before we classify them as expired?
Do we require SDKs to retry idempotent writes automatically or leave this opt-in?
risks_mitigation:
Risk: Divergent SDK semantics cause customer bugs and internal support load. Mitigation: enforce spec via automated fixtures and require passing CI tests before release.
Risk: Resume tokens leak sensitive info. Mitigation: require opaque base64 tokens signed server-side; do not include PII in token payloads.
Risk: Long-running streams overwhelm client memory when using pipeline transforms. Mitigation: provide guidance for memory-bounded transforms and require backpressure APIs in clients.
notes:
- Include sample 'migration-helper' utility in the test repo to translate tokens when servers rotate token format.
- Align with Console team on traces for resume attempts so we can detect systematic mid-stream failures.
- Schedule architecture review with Runtime team week of 2026-03-22.
